title: Panoramic dental X-ray (OPG)
what: One image shows all your teeth, both jaws, and the nearby bones at once.
why: Before dental treatment and extractions, before implants and braces, and to find hidden infection and wisdom teeth.
duration: usually 5 minutes; the image itself takes 10 to 20 seconds; you get the image right away
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If the X-ray is for a child, say their age. The settings will be adjusted

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off earrings, necklaces, face piercings, hair clips, glasses, and removable dentures.

bring: Your dentist's referral, if you have one
steps: A protective apron is put on you
You step into the machine and bite on a plastic piece
You close your lips and press your tongue to the roof of your mouth
The machine slowly moves around your head. Stand still
The image appears on the screen right away
feel: You just stand for 10 to 20 seconds
after: You usually get the image right away, on a disc, a USB drive, or by email

faq.q: How much radiation is in a panoramic X-ray?
faq.a: The dose is small, about the same as a few days of normal natural background radiation.

faq.q: How is a panoramic X-ray different from a dental CT?
faq.a: A panoramic X-ray is a flat picture of all the teeth. A CT is 3D and more detailed. It is ordered for implants and complex cases.

reminders.text: Panoramic dental X-ray soon. Take off earrings and piercings, and bring past X-rays.
